## Summary

Read the vignette 'Basic estimation on simulated data' before reading this. 
Here we build upon the simpler vignette by showing how to do simulation and inference with regression models for the five parameters of the mixture model for x: p_pos (seroprevalence), mu_pos and mu_neg (the mean x for seropositives and seronegatives), sd_pos and sd_neg (the standard deviation for seropositives and seronegatives).

## Setting up

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(dvsb)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_classic())
```

## Simulate data

Let's simulate a population comprised of different jobs and places.
p_pos varies by place (a lot) and job (a little); the other parameters vary a little by place.

```{r simulate, message=FALSE}
places <- c("north", "south", "east", "west")
jobs <- c("office", "farmer", "none")
data <- simulate_data(seed = 12345,
                      num_plate = 30,
                      x_mix_pred_vars = list(
                        p_pos = list(place = places, job = jobs),
                        mu_pos = list(place = places),
                        mu_neg = list(place = places),
                        sd_pos = list(place = places),
                        sd_neg = list(place = places)),
                      x_mix_pred_vars_sds = list(
                        p_pos = c(place = 1, job = 0.1),
                        mu_pos = c(place = 0.1),
                        mu_neg = c(place = 0.1),
                        sd_pos = c(place = 0.1),
                        sd_neg = c(place = 0.1)))
df_sam <- data$df_sam
df_cal <- data$df_cal
df_plate <- data$df_plate
param_true_values_list <- data$params
x_mix_pred_vars_names <- data$x_mix_pred_vars_names
```

Plot the simulated sample data, first histogramming the x values, stratifying by the distinct subpopulations:

```{r plot_data_sam_x, fig.height=5}
ggplot(df_sam) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = x), bins = 20) +
  facet_grid(place ~ job) +
  scale_x_log10()
```

And show the distributions of the y values too:

```{r plot_data_sam_y, fig.height=5}
# With default values, y is rarely negative; restrict to positive for visibility
ggplot(df_sam %>% filter(y > 0)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = y), bins = 20) +
  facet_grid(place ~ job) +
  scale_x_log10()
```

## Run Stan

Prepare for and run Stan as we did in the simpler vignette.

```{r stan, error = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, results = "hide"}
priors_list <- get_priors()

data_wrangled <- wrangle_data(
  df_sam = df_sam, 
  df_cal = df_cal, 
  priors_list = priors_list,
  x_mix_pred_vars_names = x_mix_pred_vars_names
)

df_sam <- data_wrangled$df_sam
df_cal <- data_wrangled$df_cal
df_plate <- dplyr::left_join(df_plate, data_wrangled$df_plate, by = "plate") 

capture.output({
df_posterior <- run_stan(data_wrangled = data_wrangled)
df_prior <- run_stan(data_wrangled = data_wrangled, distribution = "prior")
})
```

## Analyse Stan output

For each of the population-level parameters we plot the posterior, prior and true value, just for 16 parameters for better visibility.

```{r plot_posterior_prior, warning=FALSE, out.width="95%", fig.height=7}
param_true_values_vector <- wrangle_true_params(
  param_true_values_list = param_true_values_list,
  data_descriptors = data_wrangled$data_descriptors)

mastiff::plot_posterior(
    posterior_samples = df_posterior,
    prior_samples     = df_prior,
    params_desired = names(df_prior)[1:16],
    true_param_values = param_true_values_vector,
    skip_stanfit_to_dt = TRUE)
```


`df_posterior` has columns named `y_sam_sim_unconditional[1]`, `y_sam_sim_unconditional[2]` etc. which contain posterior predicted y values for new set of sampled individuals with the same distribution of covariates (i.e. partitioned into the same subpopulations, in this example based on job and place) as in the dataset analysed.
The integer in square brackets indexes the sample replicate as in `df_sam$which_sam_rep`; we merge `df_sam` into `df_posterior` to associate each predicted `y` value with the appropriate subpopulation.
We plot the subpopulation-level distributions of y values: the empirical distribution in blue, and the posterior predictive distribution in black.

```{r plot_posterior_retrodictive, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_y_sim <- df_posterior %>%
  select(starts_with("y_sam_sim_unconditional[")) %>%
  filter(row_number() %% 10 == 0) %>% # downsample for speed
  mutate(sample = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c("sample"), names_to = "param") %>%
  tidyr::extract(param, 
               into = "which_sam_rep", 
               regex = "y_sam_sim_unconditional\\[([0-9]+)\\]") %>%
  mutate(which_sam_rep = as.integer(which_sam_rep)) %>%
  left_join(df_sam, by = "which_sam_rep") %>%
  mutate(value = log10(value))
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = df_y_sim,
               aes(x = value,
                   group = sample),
               color = "black") +
  geom_density(data = df_sam,
            aes(x = log10(y)),
            color="blue") +
  coord_cartesian(expand = F) +
  facet_grid(place ~ job, scale = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "log10(OD value)",
       y = "probability density") +
  xlim(-3, NA)
```

## Subtleties of seroprevalence when stratified

As discussed in the supplementary information section 'Subtleties of seroprevalence when stratified' of the dvsb scientific article, there are (at least) two ways of estimating seroprevalence in subpopulation stratifications.
The first is a 'purely parametric' estimator, obtained by adding the overall `p_pos` parameter and all the regression coefficients associated with the covariates for `p_pos`, marginalising over any covariates you want to disregard in the definition of your subpopulation of interest, and finally taking the posterior distribution of the resulting quantity.
The second is posterior predicted seroprevalence for a hypothetical new dataset of exactly the same size and subpopulation composition as the one sampled.
Algorithmically, we arrive at this by making a posterior prediction for a new serostatus for each sampled individual, conditioning on which subpopulation they are in.
This is what's done in dvsb to produce the parameters named `pos_sam_sim_unconditional[...]` with an integer index for the individual in the square brackets.
We can then group the individuals however we desire, calculate the seroprevalence within the group, and then calculate the posterior distribution for this quantity.
We illustrate this below.

First extract from `df_posterior` the prediction, for each individual and each sample from the posterior, the predicted positivity (0 or 1).
Link this back to each individual's covariates: place and job.

```{r stratified_seroprevalence_1}
df_is_pos_sim <- df_posterior %>%
  select(starts_with("pos_sam_sim_unconditional[")) %>%
  mutate(sample = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -sample, values_to = "pos") %>%
  tidyr::extract(name, 
                 into = "id_sam_int", 
                 regex = "pos_sam_sim_unconditional\\[([0-9]+)\\]") %>%
  mutate(id_sam_int = as.integer(id_sam_int)) %>%
  left_join(df_sam %>% 
              select(id_sam_int, place, job) %>% 
              distinct(),
            by = "id_sam_int")
```

Then calculate quantiles of the posterior predictive distribution for seroprevalence when stratifying the population in different ways.

```{r stratified_seroprevalence_2}
quantiles <- c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)

# Stratify by place only
df_seroprevalence_sim_by_place <- df_is_pos_sim %>%
  summarise(.by = c("place", "sample"), seroprevalence = mean(pos)) %>%
  group_by(place) %>%
  reframe(seroprevalence = quantile(seroprevalence, probs = quantiles),
          quantile = quantiles) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = quantile,
              names_prefix = "quantile_",
              values_from = seroprevalence)

# Stratify by job only
df_seroprevalence_sim_by_job <- df_is_pos_sim %>%
  summarise(.by = c("job", "sample"), seroprevalence = mean(pos)) %>%
  group_by(job) %>%
  reframe(seroprevalence = quantile(seroprevalence, probs = quantiles),
          quantile = quantiles) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = quantile,
              names_prefix = "quantile_",
              values_from = seroprevalence)

# Stratify by place and job simultaneously
df_seroprevalence_sim_by_place_job <- df_is_pos_sim %>%
  summarise(.by = c("place", "job", "sample"), seroprevalence = mean(pos)) %>%
  group_by(place, job) %>%
  reframe(seroprevalence = quantile(seroprevalence, probs = quantiles),
          quantile = quantiles) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = quantile,
              names_prefix = "quantile_",
              values_from = seroprevalence)
```

Because this is simulated data, we can also calculate the true seroprevalence that was sampled in each of these stratifications.

```{r stratified_seroprevalence_3}
df_is_pos_true <- df_sam %>% 
  select(id_sam, place, job, pos) %>% 
  distinct()
df_seroprevalence_true_by_place <- df_is_pos_true %>%
  summarise(.by = place, seroprevalence = mean(pos))
df_seroprevalence_true_by_job <- df_is_pos_true %>%
  summarise(.by = job, seroprevalence = mean(pos))
df_seroprevalence_true_by_place_job <- df_is_pos_true %>%
  summarise(.by = c("place", "job"), seroprevalence = mean(pos))
```

Plot the predicted seroprevalence (black point and error bars, for the posterior median and central 95%) and the true seroprevalence (blue point) for each of the strata:

```{r stratified_seroprevalence_plot}
ggplot(data = df_seroprevalence_sim_by_place) +
  geom_point(aes(place, quantile_0.5)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(place, ymin = quantile_0.025, ymax = quantile_0.975)) +
  geom_point(data = df_seroprevalence_true_by_place,
             aes(place, seroprevalence), col = "blue") +
  labs(y = "seroprevalence") +
  ylim(0, 1)

ggplot(data = df_seroprevalence_sim_by_job) +
  geom_point(aes(job, quantile_0.5)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(job, ymin = quantile_0.025, ymax = quantile_0.975)) +
  geom_point(data = df_seroprevalence_true_by_job,
             aes(job, seroprevalence), col = "blue") +
  labs(y = "seroprevalence") +
  ylim(0, 1)

ggplot(data = df_seroprevalence_sim_by_place_job) +
  geom_point(aes(job, quantile_0.5)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(job, ymin = quantile_0.025, ymax = quantile_0.975)) +
  geom_point(data = df_seroprevalence_true_by_place_job,
             aes(job, seroprevalence), col = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~place) +
  labs(y = "seroprevalence") +
  ylim(0, 1)
```
